intent.raw_query: Cambodia Angkor Wat + beaches, $1100, 10 days, November 2026

selected_hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Angkor Wat Temple Complex Sunrise Tour
experiences.description: Explore the world's largest religious monument at sunrise, wandering through the iconic towers and intricate bas-reliefs of the 12th-century Khmer Empire. Hire a local tuk-tuk driver for a full-day pass covering Angkor Wat, Bayon, and Ta Prohm temples.

experiences.name: Phnom Penh Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda Visit
experiences.description: Tour the stunning Royal Palace complex and the Silver Pagoda, home to a floor made of 5,000 silver tiles and a life-sized gold Buddha adorned with diamonds. Combine with a visit to the nearby National Museum to see the world's finest collection of Khmer art and sculpture.

experiences.name: Koh Rong Samloem Beach Escape
experiences.description: Take a ferry to this pristine island paradise featuring crystal-clear turquoise waters, white sand beaches, and vibrant coral reefs. Spend days snorkeling, kayaking, and relaxing on Saracen Bay, one of Southeast Asia's most unspoiled beaches, with bioluminescent plankton visible at night.
experiences.location: Koh Rong Samloem Island, Sihanoukville Province

experiences.name: Cambodian Street Food and Market Tour
experiences.description: Join a guided evening walk through the bustling Old Market and surrounding streets, sampling authentic Khmer dishes including fish amok, lok lak, nom banh chok (Khmer noodles), and fresh tropical fruit. Visit local stalls and learn about the cultural significance of Cambodian cuisine from a knowledgeable local guide.

experiences.name: Tonle Sap Floating Village Boat Tour
experiences.description: Cruise through the extraordinary floating villages of Kampong Phluk on Southeast Asia's largest freshwater lake. Witness the unique stilted wooden houses, floating schools, and fish farms of communities that have lived on the water for generations, offering a deeply authentic cultural immersion into rural Cambodian life.
experiences.location: Kampong Phluk, Tonle Sap Lake, Siem Reap Province

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Cambodia
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and transit time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to your boutique stay near Angkor Archaeological Park. Once settled, take a leisurely tuk-tuk ride to the nearby Angkor Thom South Gate to get your first iconic glimpse of the ancient ruins without entering the park. Stroll around the outer moat area and soak in the atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Pub Street and the Old Market (Psar Chas) area in central Siem Reap. Explore the lively night market, browse local handicrafts, and enjoy the vibrant street atmosphere as an easy first-night orientation.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or grab a snack at the airport upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick and cheap bowl of noodle soup or Khmer rice dish at a local stall near the airport or along the road to your hotel (~$2–3 USD).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Khmer Kitchen Restaurant on Pub Street — a beloved budget-friendly local spot serving authentic Khmer dishes like Amok fish curry and lok lak for $4–6 per dish.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase your Angkor Archaeological Park pass on arrival afternoon if energy allows — a 3-day pass costs $62 USD and is valid for any 3 days within a week. Tuk-tuks from the airport to the hotel should cost $6–9 USD. Negotiate fares in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early (ideally by 5:00–5:30 AM) to witness the iconic sunrise over Angkor Wat. Arrive at the main reflecting pool before dawn for the best view. Spend the morning exploring Angkor Wat's galleries, bas-reliefs depicting the Churning of the Ocean of Milk, and the central towers. This is the world's largest religious monument and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue inside the Angkor Archaeological Park to explore Angkor Thom — the ancient walled city. Visit the Bayon Temple with its 216 serene stone faces, the Baphuon Temple, Phimeanakas, and the Terrace of the Elephants. Hire a tuk-tuk driver for the day (~$15–18 USD) to navigate between sites efficiently.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your hotel to freshen up. Visit the Angkor Night Market for souvenir shopping and enjoy a traditional Apsara dance performance at a local restaurant (some offer free shows with dinner). Explore street food stalls around the market.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at your hotel or grab a baguette sandwich (a French-Cambodian legacy) and coffee from a street vendor near Angkor Wat for ~$1–2 USD.
meals.lunch: Pack snacks or eat at one of the simple local food stalls inside the park near Angkor Thom — rice with grilled chicken or fried noodles for ~$2–3 USD.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Mahob Restaurant near the Old Market — affordable Khmer cuisine with dishes like beef lok lak and Khmer red curry for $5–8 USD.

day_by_day.notes: November weather in Siem Reap is dry season — expect warm temperatures around 28–32°C. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and plenty of water. Wear modest clothing (covered shoulders and knees) to enter temple sanctuaries. Start sunrise visit with your Angkor pass in hand.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the outer temples of Angkor on the Grand Circuit. Visit Ta Prohm — the atmospheric 'jungle temple' famously featured in Tomb Raider, where massive tree roots engulf ancient stone walls. Then head to Banteay Kdei and the serene Srah Srang reservoir, a beautiful spot for quiet reflection in the early morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Preah Khan Temple, a sprawling complex of corridors and courtyards dedicated to the father of King Jayavarman VII. Then visit Neak Pean, a unique artificial island temple set in a large reservoir (accessible by a raised wooden walkway). End with the East Mebon temple.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Artisans Angkor workshop and shop in Siem Reap town — free entry, and you can watch skilled Cambodian artisans carve stone, lacquer wood, and weave silk, keeping traditional crafts alive. Browse for affordable handmade souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel or a nearby local café — try Khmer rice porridge (bobor) with ginger and egg for ~$1.50–2.50 USD.
meals.lunch: Eat at a local restaurant near Ta Prohm — opt for a set rice lunch with vegetables and protein for ~$3–4 USD.
meals.dinner: Try a local Khmer BBQ (sach ko ang) spot near the Old Market where you grill your own meats at the table — budget around $5–7 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: This is your 3rd day using your Angkor pass if you purchased a 3-day pass. If you bought a 1-day pass, today would require a new ticket. Consider a tuk-tuk for the full Grand Circuit (~$15–18 for the day). Carry insect repellent as jungle temples can have mosquitoes.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning trip to Banteay Srei, located about 25 km northeast of Siem Reap. This 10th-century temple is renowned for its intricate pink sandstone carvings — considered some of the finest examples of Khmer art. The detail of the decorative work is extraordinary and unlike anything in the main Angkor complex.
day_by_day.afternoon: On the way back, stop at the Landmine Museum (Cambodia Landmine Museum and Relief Facility) — a sobering and deeply important cultural stop that educates visitors about the devastating impact of landmines left from decades of conflict. Entry is ~$5 USD and proceeds support mine clearance and victims. Then visit the Cambodia Cultural Village for a condensed overview of Cambodia's diverse ethnic groups and traditions.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed evening at a rooftop bar or café in Siem Reap town. Visit the Siem Reap Art Center Night Market for local art, handmade goods, and street food snacks.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel or a local bakery — fresh fruit, eggs, and coffee for ~$2–3 USD.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch or eat at a simple local eatery near Banteay Srei — fried rice with vegetables and a drink for ~$2–3 USD.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Viva, a Mexican-Khmer fusion restaurant in Siem Reap offering affordable meals around $4–7 USD — a fun change of pace.

day_by_day.notes: Banteay Srei is outside the main Angkor Park boundary and does NOT require an Angkor pass — it has its own entry fee of $10 USD. Hire a tuk-tuk for the half-day trip (~$12–15 USD round trip). The ride takes about 45 minutes each way — enjoy the rural Cambodian countryside along the route.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning boat trip on Tonlé Sap Lake — Southeast Asia's largest freshwater lake and a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve. Visit the floating villages of Chong Kneas or Kampong Phluk (Kampong Phluk is more authentic and less touristy). Witness the unique way of life of communities living entirely on water — floating schools, temples, and markets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Siem Reap and visit the Angkor National Museum — an excellent indoor museum presenting the history and art of the Khmer Empire through galleries of Buddha images, royal regalia, and multimedia displays. Entry is ~$12 USD and provides great context for everything you've seen at the temples.
day_by_day.evening: Treat yourself to a traditional Khmer massage — many reputable budget massage parlors in Siem Reap offer 1-hour traditional massages for $7–10 USD. Then enjoy a quiet dinner near your hotel.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before the boat trip — rice with fried egg and fresh fruit at a local stall for ~$1.50–2 USD.
meals.lunch: Eat lunch at a floating restaurant on Tonlé Sap Lake — simple fish dishes with rice for ~$4–5 USD, or bring snacks to save money.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Bugs Café (if adventurous!) — a unique Siem Reap experience offering insect-based dishes alongside conventional Khmer food, with mains from $5–9 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Boat tours to Kampong Phluk cost approximately $15–20 USD per person including transport and boat ride — book through your hotel or a local guesthouse to avoid inflated tourist prices. The dry season (November) means lake levels are lower, which can make Kampong Phluk's stilted houses even more dramatic.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Siem Reap by bus to Phnom Penh, Cambodia's capital city. Budget bus services (Giant Ibis, Mekong Express, or Larryta) offer comfortable air-conditioned coaches for $9–15 USD and take approximately 5–6 hours. Enjoy the passing Cambodian countryside.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Phnom Penh early-to-mid afternoon. Check in to a budget guesthouse in the BKK1 or Riverside area (~$10–20 USD/night for a clean private room). Head to the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda — the stunning official residence of the Cambodian King, featuring golden spires and a floor of 5,000 silver tiles. Entry is $10 USD.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the scenic Phnom Penh Riverside promenade (Sisowath Quay) as the sun sets over the Mekong and Tonlé Sap confluence. Browse the evening street food scene along the riverfront.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast before departure in Siem Reap — grab a Khmer baguette sandwich and iced coffee from a street vendor for ~$1.50 USD.
meals.lunch: Eat lunch on the bus or at a roadside stop — simple rice dishes available for ~$2–3 USD.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a riverside restaurant in Phnom Penh — try Khmer fish amok or grilled prawns at a local eatery for $4–7 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Book your bus ticket in advance online or through your hotel the night before. Giant Ibis is highly recommended for reliability and comfort. Store your main luggage at the bus station or your new guesthouse upon arrival before sightseeing. Note that Cambodia uses both USD and Khmer Riel — USD is widely accepted.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) — a former high school converted into a torture and detention center by the Khmer Rouge regime (1975–1979). This deeply moving and historically essential museum documents the atrocities of the Khmer Rouge. Entry is $8 USD. Allow 2–3 hours for a thorough visit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a tuk-tuk (~$10–12 USD round trip) to the Choeung Ek Killing Fields Memorial, located about 15 km outside the city center. This UNESCO-listed memorial site honors the victims of the Khmer Rouge genocide. The audio guide (included in the $6 USD entry) is exceptional and deeply informative.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the city and visit the bustling Central Market (Psar Thmei) — an Art Deco landmark built in 1937 with a distinctive yellow dome. Browse stalls selling jewelry, clothing, and local goods. Have a quiet, reflective dinner near your guesthouse.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a local café near your guesthouse — Khmer-style noodle soup (kuy teav) for ~$1.50–2 USD.
meals.lunch: Light lunch near Tuol Sleng — a simple rice and vegetable dish at a local restaurant for ~$2–3 USD.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Friends Restaurant (Mith Samlanh) — a social enterprise training at-risk youth in hospitality. Excellent Khmer tapas and cocktails with mains from $4–8 USD. A meaningful place to dine.

day_by_day.notes: Today is emotionally heavy — visiting both S-21 and Choeung Ek in one day is intense but important for understanding Cambodian history. Take your time, be respectful, and allow yourself space to process. Dress modestly at these sites. Photography is permitted but approach with sensitivity.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the National Museum of Cambodia — housed in a stunning terracotta-colored Khmer-style building near the Royal Palace. It holds the world's largest collection of Khmer artifacts including the famous Jayavarman VII statue. Entry is $10 USD. Then visit Wat Phnom — the hilltop temple that gives Phnom Penh its name, free to enter (small donation expected).
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a local bus or cheap tuk-tuk to the Russian Market (Psar Tuol Tom Poung) — the best market in Phnom Penh for authentic handicrafts, silk scarves, silverware, and budget clothing. Great for picking up gifts and souvenirs at negotiable prices. Spend a couple of hours exploring the labyrinthine stalls.
day_by_day.evening: Catch a sunset cruise on the Mekong River — several local boat operators offer 1-hour sunset cruises from the Phnom Penh riverside for $5–8 USD per person. Watch the sky turn gold over the confluence of the Mekong and Tonlé Sap rivers.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a French-style bakery near the Riverside — a croissant and café au lait for ~$2–3 USD (Phnom Penh has excellent French-influenced bakeries).
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local Khmer restaurant near the Russian Market — try num banh chok (Khmer noodles) for ~$1.50–2 USD.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Romdeng Restaurant — a social enterprise serving traditional Cambodian cuisine including regional dishes rarely found elsewhere. Mains from $5–9 USD.

day_by_day.notes: The Russian Market is best visited in the morning or late afternoon to avoid peak heat. Bargaining is expected and part of the culture — start at about 50–60% of the asking price and negotiate respectfully. Keep small USD bills and Riel for market purchases.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Phnom Penh early by bus or minivan to Sihanoukville (approximately 4–5 hours, $7–10 USD). From Sihanoukville, take a ferry to Koh Rong Samloem island (~$25–30 USD round trip, 45 minutes) — one of Cambodia's most beautiful and least developed islands with pristine white sand beaches and turquoise waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Koh Rong Samloem and check in to a budget bungalow on Saracen Bay or M'Pai Bay (~$15–25 USD/night for a basic beach bungalow). Spend the afternoon swimming, snorkeling, and relaxing on the stunning beach. Rent snorkeling gear for ~$5 USD to explore the coral reefs.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the magical bioluminescent plankton in the sea after dark — Koh Rong Samloem is one of the best places in the world to see this natural phenomenon. Simply wade into the warm water at night and watch the water glow blue around you. It's free and unforgettable.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before departure in Phnom Penh — grab a banh mi sandwich and coffee from a street stall for ~$1.50 USD.
meals.lunch: Eat lunch on the ferry or at a beachside restaurant upon arrival on the island — fresh grilled fish with rice for ~$5–7 USD.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a beachfront restaurant on Saracen Bay — freshly caught seafood (grilled squid, shrimp, or fish) with rice and vegetables for $6–9 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Ferry schedules from Sihanoukville to Koh Rong Samloem typically run in the morning and early afternoon. Book your ferry ticket in advance during peak season. Sihanoukville itself has become heavily developed — skip the main town and head straight to the island. Bring cash as ATMs are limited on the island. Bring reef-safe sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for a final sunrise walk along the beach on Koh Rong Samloem. Take a morning kayak trip (~$5–8 USD/hour rental) around the island's coastline to explore hidden coves and mangroves. Alternatively, join a half-day snorkeling boat tour (~$15–20 USD) to visit nearby coral reefs and marine life.
day_by_day.afternoon: After a final swim and lunch on the island, take the afternoon ferry back to Sihanoukville. From Sihanoukville, take a bus or shared taxi back toward Phnom Penh or your onward destination. Reflect on 10 incredible days across Cambodia's history, culture, and beaches.
day_by_day.evening: If returning to Phnom Penh for a flight, arrive in the evening and enjoy a final farewell dinner in the capital. If departing from another city, arrange transport accordingly. Take one last stroll along the Phnom Penh Riverside to say goodbye to Cambodia.

meals.breakfast: Final island breakfast at your bungalow café — fresh tropical fruit plate, eggs, and coffee for ~$3–4 USD.
meals.lunch: Last beachside meal on Koh Rong Samloem — coconut curry with rice or grilled fish for ~$5–7 USD.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner in Phnom Penh at a local Khmer restaurant — order your favorite dish from the trip one last time. Budget $5–8 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Check ferry departure times carefully and arrive at the pier 30 minutes early. Keep some extra USD and Riel for departure taxes or last-minute purchases. Total estimated budget for the full 10-day trip (excluding international flights): approximately $350–500 USD per person, covering accommodation, local transport, food, and entrance fees at a comfortable budget level.

trip_options.title: Classic Cambodia Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and transit time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to your boutique stay near Angkor Archaeological Park. Freshen up, then take a gentle orientation stroll around the hotel grounds and nearby Angkor village. Visit the Angkor National Museum (open until 18:30) for a stunning introduction to Khmer history and the civilizations behind the temples — a perfect way to set context before exploring the park.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Pub Street and the Old Market (Psar Chaa) area in Siem Reap town for a lively first evening. Browse the night market stalls and soak in the atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy a light snack or meal on the plane or at the airport upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the airport or a café near the hotel after check-in — try a bowl of Khmer noodle soup (kuy teav) at a local eatery for around $3–5.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Mahob Restaurant on Pub Street — a well-regarded mid-range spot serving authentic Cambodian cuisine. Try amok trei (fish amok) and lok lak (stir-fried beef). Budget $10–15 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Exchange currency to Cambodian Riel (KHR) at the airport or a local exchange booth. USD is widely accepted. Purchase a 3-day Angkor Pass ($62) at the Angkor ticket office — it opens until 17:30 and you can use the pass starting the next morning.

day_by_day.morning: Early start for sunrise at Angkor Wat (arrive by 05:30). Watch the sun rise over the iconic five towers reflected in the lotus pond — one of Southeast Asia's most breathtaking sights. Spend the morning exploring the grand galleries, bas-reliefs depicting the Churning of the Ocean of Milk, and the central sanctuary. Hire a licensed guide at the entrance ($25–30) for rich historical context.
day_by_day.afternoon: After a mid-morning break, visit Angkor Thom — the great walled city. Explore the Bayon Temple with its 216 enigmatic stone faces, the Baphuon, the Elephant Terrace, and the Terrace of the Leper King. These are all within easy tuk-tuk distance inside the park.
day_by_day.evening: Return to town for a relaxed evening. Visit the Angkor Night Market for handicrafts and souvenirs, then enjoy a traditional Apsara dance performance dinner show.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the hotel or grab a baguette and coffee from a roadside stall near the park entrance — a French-Cambodian legacy treat for under $3.
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch near the park or eat at one of the casual restaurants inside the Angkor complex near Angkor Wat's north gate. Try a Khmer red curry with rice ($5–7).
meals.dinner: Dinner with Apsara dance show at Koulen II Restaurant or Smile of Angkor — buffet dinner with a cultural performance. Budget $15–20 per person including the show.

day_by_day.notes: November weather in Siem Reap is dry season — expect warm temperatures (25–32°C). Wear light, breathable clothing that covers shoulders and knees for temple respect. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and plenty of water. Hire a tuk-tuk driver for the full day ($15–20).

day_by_day.morning: Explore the outer temples of Angkor on the Grand Circuit. Begin with Preah Khan — a sprawling jungle temple dedicated to the father of Jayavarman VII, with atmospheric tree roots and long columned corridors. Then visit Neak Pean, a unique artificial island temple built on a circular island in a pond.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Ta Som, a small but charming temple with a famous tree-root-engulfed eastern gopura. Then visit East Mebon and the stunning Pre Rup temple — climb to the top for panoramic views over the surrounding jungle and rice fields, especially beautiful in the late afternoon golden light.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a cooking class experience in Siem Reap town. Learn to prepare 3–4 traditional Khmer dishes and eat your creations for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or at a local café — try num banh chok (Khmer rice noodles with fish gravy and fresh herbs), a classic Cambodian breakfast for $2–4.
meals.lunch: Casual lunch at a local restaurant near the Grand Circuit — try a Khmer BBQ platter or fresh spring rolls with dipping sauce ($6–8).
meals.dinner: Khmer cooking class and dinner at a reputable school such as Cambodian Cooking Class or Siem Reap Cooking Class. Budget $25–35 per person including ingredients and instruction.

day_by_day.notes: This is your last day using the 3-day Angkor Pass. The Grand Circuit covers more ground — consider renting a bicycle ($5–8/day) for a more immersive, eco-friendly experience if you're comfortable cycling in heat.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Roluos Group of Temples — among the oldest Khmer temples, predating Angkor. Explore Bakong (the first great temple mountain), Preah Ko, and Lolei. These are quieter and less touristy, offering an intimate sense of discovery. Located about 13 km southeast of Siem Reap.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Siem Reap and visit the Artisans Angkor workshop and shop at Angkor Silk Farm (free entry). Watch skilled artisans carve stone, lacquer wood, and weave silk — a living tradition of Khmer craftsmanship. Great opportunity for meaningful, ethically made souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Siem Reap's vibrant café and bar scene along the riverside. Visit the Siem Reap Art Center Night Market for local art, handmade goods, and street food.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel. If included, enjoy it fully — otherwise try a French-style café breakfast (baguette, eggs, coffee) at a nearby café for $4–6.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local restaurant in the Roluos area or back in town — try bai sach chrouk (pork and rice) at a local eatery for $2–4.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Haven Restaurant — a social enterprise training at-risk youth in hospitality. Excellent Khmer and Western fusion dishes. Budget $10–15 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Roluos Group is best visited in the morning before the heat peaks. Arrange a tuk-tuk for the round trip ($10–12). This is a free day from the Angkor Pass — no ticket needed for Roluos.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Phnom Kulen National Park (about 50 km from Siem Reap). Visit the sacred Kbal Spean River of a Thousand Lingas — a riverbed carved with hundreds of Hindu fertility symbols. Trek through lush jungle to reach the carvings and a beautiful waterfall. This is considered the sacred source of the Angkor civilization.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Phnom Kulen — visit the giant reclining Buddha carved into a natural rock formation at the hilltop pagoda, and swim in the refreshing waterfall pools (bring a swimsuit). Enjoy the scenic jungle landscape.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siem Reap in the late afternoon. Relax with a traditional Khmer massage to soothe tired muscles from the day's trekking.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure — pack snacks and water for the day.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or eat at one of the simple local food stalls near the park entrance. Basic Khmer rice dishes available for $3–5.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Cuisine Wat Damnak — one of Siem Reap's finest restaurants offering a contemporary tasting menu of Cambodian cuisine. Budget $30–40 per person for a special evening. Book ahead.

day_by_day.notes: Phnom Kulen entry fee is $20 per person. The road can be rough — hire a reliable tuk-tuk or private car ($30–40 for the day). Wear sturdy shoes for the jungle trek. Bring insect repellent. The park opens at 08:00.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take a morning bus or shared taxi from Siem Reap to Phnom Penh (approximately 6 hours by road, or 45 minutes by domestic flight). Book Giant Ibis or Mekong Express bus for a comfortable mid-range experience ($12–15). Alternatively, fly with Cambodia Angkor Air for ~$60–80.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Phnom Penh and check into a mid-range guesthouse or boutique hotel near the riverside (pre-book for this leg). Visit the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda — Cambodia's most iconic royal landmark, with stunning Khmer architecture and a floor of 5,000 silver tiles. Dress modestly (shoulders and knees covered).
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Phnom Penh Riverside Promenade at sunset. Watch locals gather for evening exercise and socializing. Explore the Foreign Correspondents' Club (FCC) rooftop for a sunset drink with views over the Tonle Sap and Mekong rivers.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel in Siem Reap before departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch on the bus (bring snacks) or stop at a roadside restaurant en route — try a simple rice and grilled fish dish for $4–6.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Romdeng Restaurant — a social enterprise serving traditional Cambodian cuisine in a beautiful colonial villa. Try the tarantula appetizer if adventurous! Budget $12–18 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book bus tickets in advance, especially on weekends. The Giant Ibis bus departs around 07:00–08:00 from Siem Reap. Store large luggage and travel light for the day. Phnom Penh accommodation is not listed in your booking — arrange separately.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) — a sobering but essential historical site documenting the Khmer Rouge atrocities of 1975–1979. Allow 2–3 hours with an audio guide or local guide for full context. This is a deeply moving and important cultural experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Choeung Ek Genocidal Center (Killing Fields), located 15 km south of the city. The memorial stupa and peaceful grounds offer a place of reflection and remembrance. Return to the city and visit the National Museum of Cambodia — home to the world's finest collection of Khmer sculpture and art.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Phnom Penh's Central Market (Psar Thmei) — a stunning Art Deco building with vendors selling everything from jewelry to street food. Enjoy the lively local atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Phnom Penh hotel or a nearby café — try a Cambodian breakfast of rice porridge (bobor) with ginger and fish for $3–5.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local restaurant near the National Museum — try a Khmer fish curry or lok lak at a mid-range restaurant for $6–9.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Malis Restaurant — upscale Khmer cuisine in an elegant garden setting. Try the tasting menu for a curated journey through Cambodian flavors. Budget $20–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Tuol Sleng entry: $5. Choeung Ek entry: $6 (includes audio guide). These sites are emotionally heavy — take your time and be respectful. Hire a tuk-tuk for the full day ($15–20) to cover both sites comfortably.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take an early morning bus or shared minivan from Phnom Penh to Sihanoukville (approximately 4–5 hours). From Sihanoukville, take a ferry to Koh Rong Samloem island — Cambodia's most beautiful and tranquil beach island. Ferry takes about 45 minutes–1 hour.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Koh Rong Samloem and check into a mid-range beach bungalow or guesthouse on Saracen Bay or M'Pai Bay. Spend the afternoon unwinding on the pristine white sand beach, swimming in the crystal-clear turquoise water, and decompressing after the historical intensity of the past days.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from the beach. After dark, look for bioluminescent plankton in the water — Koh Rong Samloem is famous for this magical natural phenomenon (best viewed by wading into the shallows in darkness).

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your Phnom Penh hotel before departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch on the ferry or at a beachside shack upon arrival on the island — fresh grilled fish or seafood fried rice for $5–8.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a beachfront restaurant on Saracen Bay — fresh catch of the day (grilled snapper, prawns, or squid) with rice and salad. Budget $10–15 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Phnom Penh to Sihanoukville bus: $10–12 (book Giant Ibis or Mekong Express). Ferry from Sihanoukville to Koh Rong Samloem: $15–20 round trip (Speed Ferry Cambodia or GTVC). Book island accommodation in advance — options are limited. Cash is king on the island; bring enough USD.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a leisurely beach morning — swim, snorkel, or kayak in the calm waters around Saracen Bay. Rent snorkeling gear ($5–8) from your guesthouse and explore the coral reefs teeming with colorful fish. Alternatively, join a half-day snorkeling boat trip around the island ($15–20).
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike across the island to the wild and undeveloped Sunset Beach on the western shore (about 45-minute jungle trail). Spend the afternoon on this secluded beach with virtually no crowds, dramatic rock formations, and spectacular views. Swim and relax in total serenity.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Saracen Bay for sunset cocktails at a beachfront bar. Enjoy a final island evening under the stars — the lack of light pollution makes stargazing extraordinary.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your guesthouse — fresh fruit platter, eggs, toast, and coffee. Budget $4–7.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from your guesthouse or snacks brought to Sunset Beach — or eat at a simple food shack near the beach trail.
meals.dinner: Beachfront BBQ dinner at your guesthouse or a neighboring restaurant — whole grilled fish with Khmer herbs, sticky rice, and fresh mango salad. Budget $12–18 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The trail to Sunset Beach can be muddy — wear sandals with grip or light hiking shoes. Bring water, sunscreen, and insect repellent. There are no facilities on Sunset Beach. November is dry season so conditions should be ideal for beach activities.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning on Koh Rong Samloem — take one last swim or sunrise walk along the beach. Pack up and take the morning ferry back to Sihanoukville. From Sihanoukville, arrange onward transport to Phnom Penh airport or Siem Reap depending on your departure flight.
day_by_day.afternoon: If time permits before your departure flight, stop in Sihanoukville briefly or transit through Phnom Penh. Visit a last-minute souvenir shop or enjoy a final Cambodian meal. If flying from Phnom Penh, the drive from Sihanoukville takes about 4 hours — plan accordingly.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Cambodia. Reflect on an incredible 10 days of temples, history, culture, and beaches — a truly balanced Cambodian adventure.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast on the island — enjoy the tropical setting one last time. Fresh coconut, fruit, and eggs at your guesthouse ($4–6).
meals.lunch: Lunch in Sihanoukville or en route — try a final bowl of Khmer noodle soup or a banh mi sandwich from a street vendor ($2–5).
meals.dinner: Airport meal or dinner in Phnom Penh if time allows before your flight — a final taste of Cambodian cuisine to remember the trip.

day_by_day.notes: Check ferry and bus schedules the night before to ensure smooth connections. Morning ferry from Koh Rong Samloem typically departs around 07:00–08:00. Allow at least 6–7 hours total travel time from island to Phnom Penh airport. Keep some USD cash for ferry and bus tickets. Confirm your return flight details and departure airport.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Cambodia Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Private airport transfer to your boutique stay in Angkor Archaeological Park. After check-in and a welcome refreshment, take a leisurely orientation walk around the hotel grounds and nearby Angkor Thom South Gate to ease into the destination. Enjoy a private briefing with your dedicated concierge to review the upcoming itinerary.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the hotel's terrace or rooftop overlooking the jungle canopy. Gentle first-night dinner at the hotel's signature restaurant to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: Enjoyed on the plane
meals.lunch: Light welcome spread arranged by the hotel upon arrival — fresh tropical fruit, Cambodian spring rolls, and chilled coconut water
meals.dinner: In-house fine dining at the boutique hotel — recommended: Khmer tasting menu featuring amok trei (fish curry in banana leaf), lok lak beef, and mango sticky rice; paired with a curated Cambodian rice wine flight

day_by_day.notes: Request a late check-in in advance. Ask the concierge to arrange a private licensed Angkor guide for Days 2–4. Confirm sunrise permits for Angkor Wat on Day 2.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn private tuk-tuk to Angkor Wat for an exclusive sunrise experience (arrive by 05:15). Watch the temple's five towers reflect in the lotus ponds as dawn breaks — one of Southeast Asia's most iconic moments. Begin a guided exploration of Angkor Wat's bas-reliefs, galleries, and central sanctuary with your expert private Egyptologist-level Khmer historian guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the enigmatic Bayon Temple at Angkor Thom — marvel at 216 serene stone faces. Explore the Elephant Terrace and Terrace of the Leper King. Return to the hotel for a private poolside lunch and a 90-minute traditional Khmer massage at the spa.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive private dinner at Mahob Restaurant (Siem Reap's celebrated heritage Khmer cuisine destination) or arrange a private candlelit dinner within the Angkor complex with special event permits — a truly once-in-a-lifetime experience.

meals.breakfast: Pre-dawn light breakfast box prepared by the hotel — croissants, fresh fruit, coffee thermos, and energy bars for the sunrise excursion
meals.lunch: Poolside à la carte lunch at the hotel — grilled barramundi, green mango salad, fresh coconut
meals.dinner: Private fine dining experience featuring royal Khmer cuisine — seven-course tasting menu with dishes inspired by ancient Angkorian court recipes; wine pairing available

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes and light breathable clothing. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and insect repellent. Angkor Wat requires covered shoulders and knees for upper levels — a sarong can be purchased at the gate.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided visit to Ta Prohm — the atmospheric 'Tomb Raider' temple dramatically engulfed by giant silk-cotton trees. Arrive early (07:00) to beat crowds. Continue to Preah Khan Temple, a vast jungle monastery with stunning moss-covered corridors and hidden chambers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Banteay Srei — the 'Citadel of Women' — a 10th-century pink sandstone masterpiece renowned for its extraordinarily intricate carvings, considered the finest in all of Khmer art. Private guided tour followed by a visit to the Landmine Museum to understand Cambodia's modern history.
day_by_day.evening: Attend an exclusive private Apsara dance performance — arrange a premium front-row dinner show at Raffles Grand Hotel d'Angkor or book a private troupe performance at your boutique hotel's courtyard.

meals.breakfast: Full Khmer and Western breakfast at the hotel — rice congee with ginger, fresh baguette (French colonial legacy), tropical fruit platter, eggs to order
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch in a shaded pavilion near Banteay Srei — gourmet hamper prepared by the hotel with sandwiches, local cheeses, fresh juices, and Cambodian sweets
meals.dinner: Dinner with Apsara performance — four-course set menu featuring Cambodian classics; fine Bordeaux or Champagne pairing

day_by_day.notes: Banteay Srei is approximately 25 km from central Siem Reap — factor 45 minutes travel time. The pink sandstone glows beautifully in afternoon light for photography. Book the Apsara performance at least 48 hours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise hot air balloon ride over the Angkor Archaeological Park — drift silently above the temple complex at dawn for breathtaking aerial views of Angkor Wat, the jungle, and the surrounding landscape. A premium, unmissable experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the lesser-known but spectacular Beng Mealea Temple — a 12th-century jungle-swallowed ruin rarely visited by tourists, offering a true Indiana Jones atmosphere. Private guided exploration with your historian. Return via the floating village of Kampong Khleang on Tonlé Sap Lake for a private boat tour.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxing evening at the hotel — indulge in a couples' or solo spa ritual (traditional Cambodian herbal compress massage, followed by a flower-petal bath). Light evening at leisure.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before balloon ride — fresh fruit, yogurt, granola, and coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium riverside restaurant near Tonlé Sap — freshwater fish amok, river prawns, lotus stem salad
meals.dinner: In-hotel private chef's table experience — watch the chef prepare a bespoke five-course Khmer-French fusion dinner in the hotel kitchen; premium wine list

day_by_day.notes: Hot air balloon rides are weather-dependent — have a backup activity ready (helicopter tour or private Angkor photography session). Book balloon at least 72 hours ahead. Beng Mealea is 68 km from Siem Reap — arrange a comfortable private vehicle.

day_by_day.morning: Private half-day cooking class with a renowned Cambodian chef — visit a local market at dawn to select fresh ingredients, then learn to prepare three signature Khmer dishes: fish amok, beef lok lak, and banana blossom salad. A deeply cultural and hands-on experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Angkor boutique hotel. Private transfer to Siem Reap Airport for a short domestic flight (approximately 1 hour) to Phnom Penh — Cambodia's vibrant capital city. Check in to the legendary Raffles Hotel Le Royal (or equivalent luxury property) and freshen up.
day_by_day.evening: Evening stroll along the Phnom Penh riverside promenade (Sisowath Quay). Cocktails at the Elephant Bar at Raffles — a storied colonial-era bar that has hosted journalists, writers, and dignitaries for over a century.

meals.breakfast: Farewell breakfast at the Angkor boutique hotel — full spread of Khmer and Western options
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Siem Reap Airport lounge or on arrival in Phnom Penh — Cambodian noodle soup (kuy teav) at a premium local restaurant
meals.dinner: Dinner at Topaz Restaurant, Phnom Penh — one of the city's finest French-Cambodian fusion establishments; excellent wine cellar; elegant colonial setting

day_by_day.notes: Reconfirm domestic flight booking. Raffles Le Royal is a heritage property — request a Garden Wing room or Grand Deluxe Suite for the most atmospheric stay. The Elephant Bar's signature 'Femme Fatale' cocktail is a must-try.

day_by_day.morning: Deeply moving private guided visit to Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) and the Choeung Ek Killing Fields Memorial — essential for understanding Cambodia's tragic 20th-century history under the Khmer Rouge. A somber but profoundly important experience, ideally with an expert historian guide who can provide full context.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the magnificent Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda — Cambodia's most opulent royal complex featuring the Emerald Buddha and the Silver Floor Pagoda. Explore the National Museum of Cambodia, home to the world's finest collection of Khmer sculpture and artifacts.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cruise on the Mekong and Tonlé Sap rivers aboard a private luxury boat — enjoy Champagne canapés as the sun sets over Phnom Penh's skyline and the confluence of the two great rivers.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Raffles Le Royal — extensive buffet with live cooking stations, fresh pastries, and tropical fruits
meals.lunch: Lunch at Malis Restaurant — celebrated Cambodian fine dining institution run by Chef Luu Meng; try the Phnom Penh noodles and Kampot pepper crab
meals.dinner: Private dinner aboard the sunset cruise boat — catered by a top Phnom Penh chef; Champagne, fresh seafood, and Khmer desserts under the stars

day_by_day.notes: The Killing Fields and Tuol Sleng are emotionally intense — allow time for reflection. Audio guides are available but a private expert guide adds invaluable context. Dress modestly for the Royal Palace (no shorts or sleeveless tops).

day_by_day.morning: Private visit to the Russian Market (Psar Toul Tom Poung) and Central Market (Psar Thmei) with a personal shopping guide — hunt for premium Cambodian silk, silver jewelry, handcrafted lacquerware, and antiques. Visit a certified fair-trade silk workshop to observe traditional weaving techniques.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private transfer from Phnom Penh to Sihanoukville (approximately 4 hours by luxury vehicle) or take a private charter flight (30 minutes) for maximum comfort. Board a private speedboat to Koh Rong Sanloem island — Cambodia's most pristine and exclusive beach destination. Check in to Song Saa Private Island Resort or Alila Villas equivalent.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome sunset drinks on your private villa's deck overlooking the Gulf of Thailand. Barefoot luxury dinner on the beach under a canopy of stars.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Raffles Le Royal before departure
meals.lunch: Gourmet lunch box in the vehicle or a stop at a premium roadside restaurant en route — Cambodian BBQ and fresh coconut
meals.dinner: Private beachside dinner at the resort — fresh catch of the day grilled over coconut husks, lobster, and tropical fruit desserts; curated wine and cocktail menu

day_by_day.notes: November is the beginning of the dry season in coastal Cambodia — expect warm, sunny weather with calm seas. Ideal beach conditions. Confirm speedboat transfer times in advance. Song Saa Private Island is one of Southeast Asia's most acclaimed eco-luxury resorts.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise yoga session on the beach or private villa deck led by the resort's in-house instructor. After a leisurely breakfast, embark on a private snorkeling or scuba diving excursion to the pristine coral reefs surrounding Koh Rong Sanloem — among the most biodiverse in Southeast Asia.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kayaking through mangrove forests and hidden lagoons. Relax on Lazy Beach or M'Pai Bay — two of the island's most secluded and stunning stretches of white sand. Afternoon spa treatment at the overwater spa pavilion — choose from a traditional Khmer herbal scrub or a deep-tissue ocean-inspired massage.
day_by_day.evening: Private bioluminescent plankton night swim — wade into the warm waters of the bay after dark to experience the magical blue glow of bioluminescent plankton (a Koh Rong signature experience). Return for a nightcap at the resort bar.

meals.breakfast: In-villa breakfast delivered at your chosen time — eggs Benedict, fresh tropical fruit, Cambodian rice porridge, specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Beach club lunch — grilled seafood skewers, fresh spring rolls, watermelon juice, and cold Angkor beer
meals.dinner: Overwater dining platform dinner — seven-course seafood tasting menu with Champagne and fine wine pairing; private service

day_by_day.notes: Bioluminescence is best experienced on moonless nights — check lunar calendar and confirm with resort. Bring reef-safe sunscreen only (mandatory at Song Saa). Diving certification required for scuba; snorkeling available for all.

day_by_day.morning: Full day of pure relaxation and exploration at leisure. Optional: private boat charter to explore uninhabited nearby islands — Koh Rong, Koh Thmei Marine Reserve, or the secluded beaches of Koh Prins. Snorkel, swim, and picnic in total privacy.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a private mixology masterclass — learn to craft traditional Cambodian-inspired cocktails using local ingredients like palm sugar, lemongrass, and Kampot pepper. Alternatively, join a sunset fishing excursion with local fishermen.
day_by_day.evening: Final island evening — private bonfire on the beach with live acoustic music arranged by the resort. Farewell cocktails and a specially curated beach dinner celebrating the journey.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely villa breakfast — full spread with fresh-baked pastries, local honey, tropical fruits, and smoothies
meals.lunch: Private picnic on an uninhabited island beach — gourmet hamper with lobster rolls, chilled Champagne, fresh fruit, and artisan chocolates
meals.dinner: Private bonfire beach dinner — whole grilled lobster, fresh oysters, Cambodian seafood curry, and a decadent dessert platter; Champagne toast

day_by_day.notes: This is a free-form day — embrace spontaneity. The resort concierge can arrange virtually any experience on short notice. Consider purchasing Kampot pepper, Cambodian silk, or local handicrafts as premium souvenirs from the resort boutique.

day_by_day.morning: Final sunrise walk along the beach or a last morning swim in the crystalline waters. Pack and prepare for departure. Enjoy a leisurely farewell breakfast with views of the Gulf of Thailand.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private speedboat transfer back to Sihanoukville mainland. Private luxury vehicle or charter flight transfer to Phnom Penh International Airport. Enjoy the airport's premium lounge with complimentary refreshments while awaiting your departure flight. Final opportunity for last-minute shopping at the airport — Cambodian silk, Kampot pepper sets, and artisan crafts.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Cambodia — carry with you extraordinary memories of ancient temples, vibrant culture, and pristine tropical paradise.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the resort — your choice of full Khmer or Western menu with fresh juices and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Premium airport lounge dining or a final Cambodian meal at a Phnom Penh airport restaurant — Cambodian fried rice with Kampot pepper and fresh herbs
meals.dinner: In-flight dining

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for check-in and security. Confirm all transfers and flight details with your concierge the evening before. Declare any purchased antiques or artifacts at customs — the resort can advise on documentation. Consider leaving a gratuity for your guide, driver, and hotel staff — it is customary and greatly appreciated in Cambodia.
